content:
[0] Technology reporter Joanna Stern wrote an article last month about discovering ten pirated versions of her book 'I Am Not a Robot' on Apple Books within days of its official release. Although she successfully had these counterfeit books taken down, new fake titles quickly appeared.

[1] *New York Times* reporter Kashmir Hill discovered a fake biography about herself on Amazon, and found that there were thousands of such AI-generated biographies on the platform, all available for purchase...

[2] Stern found that most of the counterfeit books used AI-generated content to summarise her book, paired with fake authors and fake publishers.

[3] In total, I found ten obviously AI-generated ebooks riding on the coattails of my book, with covers also created by AI that mimicked the style of my original book — the same blue, yellow, and red colour scheme. Most were priced at $9.99, but some sold for as much as $20.99. So I bought a few to see how similar they were to the original. The Sophie Mercer version was basically an AI-generated content summary, with chapters and structure very similar to mine. From what I've seen, these counterfeit books and similar works seem designed to trick readers into thinking they're the original — or at least a summarised version of it.

[4] She said she successfully got Apple to take down those fake books, but three more counterfeits quickly appeared.

[5] Hill found that her own biography was riddled with errors, and even the listed author and photos were fake.

[6] Counting both Apple Books and Amazon, there now appear to be tens of thousands of low-quality AI-generated fake books online. Hill traced the people making these AI biographies, and one of them said they could produce a similar book using ChatGPT in just a few hours.

[7] The problem isn't limited to ebooks: Amazon offers print-on-demand services for authors, meaning it's essentially free to publish a paperback.

[8] 9to5Mac's take

[9] From social media posts to books, we're seeing the footprint of low-quality AI-generated content everywhere, and the problem will only get worse. For now, the most practical advice seems to be to carefully check reviews and sample chapters before purchasing a book.
